item.content:encoded:
The National Disaster Management Centre (NDMC), through the Department of Cooperative Governance (DCoG), has opened applications for its 2027 Bursary Programme, providing an opportunity for qualifying students who intend to pursue studies in disaster management, fire technology, or fire engineering at recognised public higher education institutions in South Africa.

The NDMC bursary is aimed at supporting students pursuing relevant qualifications that contribute to the development of skills and expertise in disaster risk management and fire-related fields. The opportunity covers selected undergraduate and postgraduate-level programmes for the 2027 academic year.

Students who meet the stated academic and eligibility requirements are encouraged to prepare their supporting documents and submit their applications before the closing date.

2027 NDMC Bursary Programme

The Department of Cooperative Governance (DCoG), through the National Disaster Management Centre (NDMC), is inviting applications from qualifying students for the 2027 academic year.

The bursary is specifically intended for students who plan to study a qualifying programme in:

  • Disaster Management
  • Fire Technology
  • Fire Engineering

Eligible applicants may pursue an Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma, Advanced Diploma, or full Master’s programme, provided that the programme falls within the relevant fields and is offered by a recognised public higher education institution in South Africa.

The programme does not include certificate qualifications or PhD programmes.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to students seeking to build academic and professional careers in areas associated with disaster preparedness, disaster risk reduction, emergency management, fire safety, fire technology, fire engineering and related areas.

What Is the NDMC Bursary?

The NDMC Bursary Programme is an educational funding opportunity administered through the National Disaster Management Centre under the Department of Cooperative Governance.

The programme is designed around academic programmes relevant to disaster management and fire-related disciplines. By supporting students in these fields, the initiative seeks to contribute to the development of individuals with the knowledge and skills required in areas connected to disaster management and fire services.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their intended qualification is directly aligned with one of the fields specified in the bursary advertisement before submitting an application.

Fields of Study Covered

The 2027 NDMC bursary focuses on qualifications in the following broad study areas:

1. Disaster Management

Students interested in disaster management may consider eligible programmes dealing with areas such as disaster risk reduction, disaster preparedness, emergency management, disaster response, recovery, resilience and related disaster management disciplines.

Applicants should verify that their specific programme is recognised as a qualifying Disaster Management qualification under the bursary requirements.

2. Fire Technology

The bursary also welcomes qualifying students pursuing Fire Technology programmes.

Fire Technology is relevant to the technical and operational aspects of fire prevention, fire protection and fire-related safety systems.

Students interested in this area should confirm that their chosen qualification meets the NDMC’s requirements.

3. Fire Engineering

Students pursuing qualifying Fire Engineering programmes may also apply.

Fire Engineering involves technical and engineering approaches to fire safety, fire prevention, fire protection and related areas.

As with the other fields, applicants should ensure that their qualification is offered by a recognised public higher education institution in South Africa and meets the requirements of the bursary programme.

Qualifications Covered by the Bursary

The NDMC states that applicants may pursue several levels of qualification during the 2027 academic year.

These include:

  • Undergraduate programmes
  • Post-Graduate Diploma programmes
  • Advanced Diploma programmes
  • Full Master’s programmes

However, there are important exclusions.

The bursary does not cover:

  • Certificate qualifications
  • PhD qualifications

Applicants considering programmes outside the listed qualification levels should carefully check the official bursary advertisement before applying.

Minimum Academic Requirements

Academic performance is an important requirement for the 2027 NDMC Bursary Programme.

Applicants must provide their most recent academic results, statement of results or academic transcript.

The stated minimum averages are:

Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants

Applicants for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma programmes must have a minimum average of 60%.

Master’s applicants

Applicants applying for Master’s-level study must have a minimum average of 65%.

This means prospective applicants should carefully review their latest academic results before beginning the application process.

Meeting the minimum academic average does not necessarily guarantee selection, as applicants must also satisfy the other requirements of the bursary programme and provide all requested documentation.

Supporting Documents Required

Applicants are required to submit supporting documentation together with their bursary application.

The NDMC application system specifies the documents that should be attached and downloaded underneath the application form in the required sequence.

Applicants should prepare the following documents:

1. Certified Copy of South African Identity Document

Applicants must provide a certified copy of their South African Identity Document.

The document should meet the certification requirements specified for the application.

Prospective applicants should make sure that the copy is clear and legible before uploading it.

2. Certified Copy of Matric Certificate

A certified copy of the applicant’s Matric Certificate is also required.

Applicants should ensure that the document is properly certified and that all relevant information can be clearly read.

3. Most Recent Academic Results

Applicants must provide their most recent academic results, statement of results or academic transcript.

This document is particularly important because the NDMC specifies minimum academic averages for different qualification levels.

The requirement is:

  • 60% minimum average for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants.
  • 65% minimum average for Master’s applicants.

Applicants should therefore submit their most recent available academic record.

4. Proof of Application, Acceptance or Registration

Applicants must also provide proof of application, acceptance or registration.

This document should demonstrate the applicant’s status with the relevant higher education institution.

Depending on the applicant’s circumstances, this may be proof that they have applied to, been accepted by, or registered with the relevant institution.

Applicants should make sure that the document clearly identifies the institution and the relevant programme.

5. Curriculum Vitae for Master’s Applicants

Master’s applicants are required to provide a brief Curriculum Vitae (CV).

The CV must be no longer than two pages.

This requirement specifically applies to Master’s applicants, so applicants at other qualification levels should pay attention to the distinction in the application requirements.

A concise CV should focus on relevant academic background, experience, skills, achievements and other information that may demonstrate the applicant’s suitability for postgraduate study.

6. Master’s Research Proposal

Applicants applying for Master’s programmes must also submit a research proposal.

The research proposal must focus on one of the 16 Priority Thematic Areas identified by the NDMC.

This is an important requirement for Master’s applicants and should not be overlooked.

Applicants should review the official research agenda and ensure that their proposed research topic falls within one of the specified priority thematic areas.

16 Priority Thematic Areas for Master’s Research

Master’s applicants are required to develop their research proposal around one of the NDMC’s 16 Priority Thematic Areas.

Prospective Master’s students should therefore review the official research agenda before preparing their proposal.

The research agenda is available through the NDMC bursary application system and should be consulted carefully to understand the priority areas and ensure that the proposed research is appropriately aligned.

Applicants can access the NDMC Research Agenda through the official application system’s research agenda document.

Where Can Successful Applicants Study?

The bursary is intended for qualifying programmes offered at a recognised Public Higher Institution of South Africa.

Applicants should therefore pay close attention to the type of institution they intend to attend.

The information provided by the NDMC specifically refers to recognised public higher education institutions in South Africa.

Students should verify the status of their institution and programme before submitting an application.

Important Application Deadline

The deadline for the 2027 NDMC Bursary application has been updated.

Application deadline: 30 September 2026 at 23:59.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their applications.

Preparing documents such as certified identification, Matric certificates, academic transcripts, proof of university application or registration and, where applicable, a Master’s research proposal can take time.

It is therefore advisable to begin the application process early and ensure that all required documents have been correctly prepared and uploaded before the deadline.

Important: The Application System Does Not Support Mobile Devices

One of the most important technical instructions provided by the NDMC is that the application system does not support mobile devices.

The notice specifically states that the system does not support:

  • Android devices
  • Apple devices

Applicants should therefore avoid relying on a smartphone or tablet to complete their application.

Instead, applicants should use a desktop or laptop computer to access and complete the online application.

This is particularly important because attempting to submit an application through an unsupported device could result in technical difficulties or prevent the applicant from completing the process successfully.

How to Apply for the 2027 NDMC Bursary

Applicants who meet the requirements can apply through the NDMC Bursary Management System.

Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility

Before beginning the application, confirm that:

  • You are applying for the 2027 academic year.
  • Your intended programme is in Disaster Management, Fire Technology or Fire Engineering.
  • Your qualification falls within the eligible qualification levels.
  • Your institution is a recognised public higher education institution in South Africa.
  • You meet the applicable academic average requirement.
  • You have the required supporting documentation.

Step 2: Prepare Your Supporting Documents

Prepare the required documents before starting the online application.

These include:

  1. Certified South African Identity Document.
  2. Certified Matric Certificate.
  3. Most recent academic results, statement or transcript.
  4. Proof of application, acceptance or registration.
  5. Two-page maximum CV for Master’s applicants.
  6. Master’s research proposal aligned with one of the 16 Priority Thematic Areas, where applicable.

Having the documents ready in advance can make the application process easier and reduce the risk of submitting an incomplete application.

Step 3: Access the NDMC Bursary Application System

Applications are submitted online through the NDMC Bursary Management System.

Applicants should use a supported computer rather than an Android or Apple mobile device.

 

Step 4: Complete the Application Form

Applicants should provide accurate information when completing the online application.

Make sure that information entered into the application corresponds with the information contained in the supporting documents.

Step 5: Upload the Required Documents

Upload the requested supporting documents according to the instructions provided by the NDMC.

Applicants should check that:

  • Documents are clear and readable.
  • Certified copies are properly certified.
  • The correct academic record has been provided.
  • Proof of application, acceptance or registration is included.
  • Master’s applicants include their CV and research proposal.
  • All required attachments have been submitted.

Step 6: Submit Before the Deadline

Once the application has been completed and all supporting documents have been uploaded, submit it before:

30 September 2026 at 23:59.

Applicants should avoid leaving submission until the last minute because technical problems, internet connectivity issues or missing documents could prevent timely submission.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity is particularly relevant to students who are planning to build academic and professional careers in disaster management, fire technology or fire engineering.

It may be suitable for:

  • Students pursuing eligible Undergraduate qualifications.
  • Students pursuing eligible Post-Graduate Diplomas.
  • Students pursuing eligible Advanced Diplomas.
  • Students pursuing eligible Master’s programmes.
  • Students interested in disaster management and related disciplines.
  • Students interested in fire technology.
  • Students interested in fire engineering.
  • Master’s applicants whose proposed research can be aligned with one of the NDMC’s 16 Priority Thematic Areas.

Applicants should nevertheless review the complete official requirements before applying.

Why This Opportunity Is Important

Disaster management and fire-related fields play an important role in protecting communities, infrastructure and public safety.

Training professionals in these disciplines can contribute to areas such as:

  • Disaster preparedness
  • Disaster risk reduction
  • Emergency planning
  • Disaster response
  • Recovery and resilience
  • Fire prevention
  • Fire safety
  • Fire protection
  • Fire engineering
  • Public safety
  • Risk management

For students interested in these areas, pursuing a relevant qualification can provide an opportunity to develop specialised knowledge that can be applied in government, emergency services, disaster management structures, fire services, private organisations, research institutions and other related sectors.

Tips for a Strong NDMC Bursary Application

Applicants can take several practical steps to reduce avoidable mistakes.

Check your academic average

Make sure your latest academic results meet the relevant threshold before applying.

Remember:

  • 60% minimum for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants.
  • 65% minimum for Master’s applicants.

Verify your programme

Do not assume that every programme with a similar title will automatically qualify.

Confirm that your intended programme falls within the specified areas of Disaster Management, Fire Technology or Fire Engineering.

Prepare certified documents early

Certification can take time, particularly when several documents are required.

Prepare your certified copies well before the deadline.

Master’s applicants should start their research proposal early

A Master’s research proposal requires considerably more preparation than simply completing an online form.

Applicants should first review the 16 Priority Thematic Areas and then develop a research proposal that clearly aligns with one of them.

Keep the Master’s CV within the required length

The NDMC specifies a maximum of two pages for the Master’s applicant CV.

Avoid submitting an unnecessarily long CV.

Use a computer

Because the application system does not support Android or Apple mobile devices, applicants should complete the application using a suitable desktop or laptop computer.

Do not wait until the final hours

The deadline is 30 September 2026 at 23:59.

Submitting early gives applicants more time to address technical issues or correct missing information.

Official Application Link

Applicants can access the online application through the hNDMC Bursary Management System.

Applicants can also access the official 2027 Bursary Advertisement through the NDMC system

Visit the OFY Website HERE for more Bursary opportunities

 

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Opportunity 2027 NDMC Bursary
Administered by National Disaster Management Centre (NDMC)
Department Department of Cooperative Governance (DCoG)
Academic year 2027
Study fields Disaster Management, Fire Technology, Fire Engineering
Qualification levels Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma, Advanced Diploma and Master’s
Undergraduate/PG Diploma/Advanced Diploma minimum 60% average
Master’s minimum 65% average
Master’s CV Maximum 2 pages
Master’s research proposal Required
Research requirement Must align with one of 16 Priority Thematic Areas
Institution Recognised Public Higher Institution of South Africa
Certificates Excluded
PhD Excluded
Application method Online
Mobile application Not supported on Android or Apple devices
Deadline 30 September 2026 at 23:59

Final Thoughts

The 2027 NDMC Bursary Programme presents an opportunity for qualifying students interested in disaster management, fire technology and fire engineering to pursue relevant higher education programmes at recognised public higher education institutions in South Africa.

The opportunity covers Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma, Advanced Diploma and full Master’s programmes, while certificate and PhD qualifications are excluded. Applicants must also meet the applicable academic requirements, with a minimum average of 60% for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants and 65% for Master’s applicants.

Master’s applicants have additional requirements, including a maximum two-page CV and a research proposal based on one of the NDMC’s 16 Priority Thematic Areas.

Most importantly, applicants should take note of the 30 September 2026 at 23:59 deadline and the instruction that the online application system does not support Android or Apple mobile devices.

Prospective applicants should prepare their documents early, carefully review the requirements, use a supported computer to complete the application and submit all required information before the closing time.

item.content:encoded:
The Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship in the Humanities 2027–28 at Simon Fraser University (SFU) is now accepting applications from emerging and established academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers working in the humanities and arts.

Hosted by the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences (FASS) at Simon Fraser University in British Columbia, Canada, the fellowship provides an opportunity for talented and engaged individuals to develop a meaningful project within an academic and intellectual environment.

The fellowship supports creative practice and publicly engaged scholarship while encouraging applicants to explore major concerns affecting society and contribute to conversations around decolonization, Indigenization, culture, creativity and social change.

For scholars, artists, writers, knowledge keepers and practitioners whose work connects intellectual inquiry with creative practice or public engagement, the Shadbolt Fellowship offers an opportunity to develop an important project while becoming part of the Simon Fraser University community.

About the Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship

The Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship in the Humanities is supported by the Jack and Doris Shadbolt Endowment for the Humanities.

The fellowship reflects the vision of Jack and Doris Shadbolt, who viewed the humanities and arts as deeply connected to the natural and social worlds inhabited by artists, scholars and thinkers.

The programme seeks to promote the humanities and arts as important sites of:

  • Creative practice
  • Critical engagement
  • Public scholarship
  • Cultural reflection
  • Intellectual inquiry
  • Social engagement
  • Decolonization
  • Indigenization
  • Creative world-making
  • Engagement with major concerns of contemporary society

Rather than restricting the fellowship to traditional academic research, SFU takes a broad approach to the humanities and arts. Potential fellows may be academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners or writers.

This makes the opportunity relevant to individuals working across a wide range of intellectual, artistic, cultural and publicly engaged fields.

2027–28 Fellowship Opportunity

The Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences at Simon Fraser University is inviting applications for the 2027–28 academic year.

Applicants are expected to propose a project that they intend to undertake during the fellowship.

The proposed project should be clearly explained and demonstrate why the applicant’s work would benefit from a fellowship at Simon Fraser University.

Applicants should clearly communicate:

  1. The project they intend to undertake.
  2. The purpose and importance of the project.
  3. What they hope to accomplish during the fellowship.
  4. How the project relates to the humanities and/or arts.
  5. Their preferred primary unit affiliation within FASS.
  6. Any desired secondary affiliation within SFU.
  7. The length of fellowship they are requesting.
  8. Why the requested fellowship duration is appropriate for the project.

Who Can Apply?

The Shadbolt Fellowship is intended for emerging or established engaged academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers in the humanities and arts.

Potential applicants may include people whose work involves:

  • Humanities research
  • Arts and creative practice
  • Writing
  • Cultural knowledge
  • Public scholarship
  • Community-based intellectual work
  • Creative research
  • Socially engaged artistic practice
  • Critical humanities scholarship
  • Indigenous knowledge and cultural practice
  • Interdisciplinary humanities and arts projects
  • Publicly engaged research and creative work

The fellowship is therefore not limited exclusively to conventional university academics.

Emerging Applicants

The programme welcomes emerging scholars, artists, writers, practitioners and knowledge keepers.

Applicants who are at an earlier stage of their careers may be considered if they have a strong project and demonstrate the experience and preparation necessary to undertake it.

Established Applicants

Established scholars, artists, practitioners, writers and knowledge keepers are also eligible to apply.

The programme seeks a diverse group of resident fellows representing different stages of professional and intellectual development.

International Applicants

The official announcement does not specify a nationality or citizenship restriction.

Therefore, the opportunity is not presented as being limited to Canadian citizens or residents.

Applicants from outside Canada may apply if they satisfy the fellowship’s eligibility requirements and are suitable candidates.

This means applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, the Caribbean, Oceania and other regions may consider applying.

International applicants should, however, separately consider any immigration, visa, travel or residency requirements that may apply if they are selected.

Indigenous Applicants Are Particularly Encouraged

The Shadbolt Fellowship has a specific commitment to decolonization and Indigenization.

SFU states that the programme especially welcomes Indigenous applicants.

The fellowship is not restricted to Indigenous applicants, but the university’s commitment means that Indigenous scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers are particularly encouraged to submit applications.

Applicants whose proposed projects engage meaningfully with Indigenous knowledge, decolonization, Indigenization or related areas may find strong alignment with the programme’s stated mission.

Commitment to Equity, Inclusion and Diversity

The selection of resident Shadbolt Fellows will be guided by considerations of equity, inclusion and diversity.

SFU also aims to ensure that its group of resident fellows represents a broad range of humanities and arts areas.

The fellowship seeks to include:

  • Indigenous applicants
  • Emerging scholars and practitioners
  • Established scholars and practitioners
  • Academic scholars
  • Artists
  • Knowledge keepers
  • Practitioners
  • Writers
  • Applicants working across different humanities and arts disciplines

Candidates belonging to underrepresented groups are particularly encouraged to apply.

These groups include:

  • Indigenous peoples
  • Persons with disabilities
  • Racialized persons
  • Women
  • People representing gender and sexual diversity

Applicants should nevertheless focus on presenting a strong project, relevant experience and a clear explanation of why SFU is an appropriate environment for their work.

What Does the Fellowship Support?

The Shadbolt Fellowship is designed to support projects that contribute to the humanities and arts as important spaces for creative practice and critical engagement with major concerns of our times.

The programme aims to support work that can help society imagine better ways of understanding and shaping the world.

Supported approaches may include:

  • Creative arts
  • Humanities research
  • Publicly engaged scholarship
  • Critical inquiry
  • Cultural work
  • Intellectual engagement
  • Creative practice
  • Socially engaged projects
  • Decolonization
  • Indigenization
  • Interdisciplinary work

Applicants should focus on the project they intend to undertake during the fellowship rather than simply describing their previous accomplishments.

Their previous work should instead demonstrate their preparation and ability to successfully undertake the proposed project.

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit a complete application package containing the required documents.

The application should include:

1. Completed Application Form

Applicants must complete the official Shadbolt Fellowship Application Form for the 2027–28 academic year.

The application form provides the required structure for the submission and should be completed accurately and thoroughly.

2. Current CV

Applicants must provide a current curriculum vitae.

The CV should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s academic, artistic, professional, creative and/or public engagement background.

Depending on the applicant’s field, relevant information may include:

  • Education
  • Academic appointments
  • Research experience
  • Publications
  • Books
  • Articles
  • Creative works
  • Exhibitions
  • Performances
  • Professional experience
  • Awards
  • Fellowships
  • Community engagement
  • Public scholarship
  • Artistic achievements
  • Presentations
  • Relevant projects
  • Other professional or intellectual accomplishments

3. Cover Letter

Applicants must also submit a cover letter.

The cover letter should specifically address three areas identified by Simon Fraser University:

  • The project the applicant intends to undertake during the fellowship.
  • The desired primary unit affiliation in the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences and, where applicable, a secondary unit affiliation.
  • The length of fellowship desired and why that duration is appropriate.

Applicants should therefore avoid submitting a generic cover letter.

The letter should be tailored specifically to the Shadbolt Fellowship and explain the applicant’s proposed project, experience and connection to SFU.

Choosing an SFU Primary Affiliation

An important part of the application is identifying the academic unit where the applicant would like to be primarily affiliated.

The primary affiliation should be within the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences.

Applicants should consider which department or programme best matches their proposed project and intellectual interests.

A suitable affiliation can help demonstrate that the applicant has carefully considered how their work would fit within SFU’s academic environment.

Secondary Unit Affiliation

Applicants may also identify a secondary affiliation if appropriate.

Importantly, SFU states that secondary units may be any unit within Simon Fraser University and are not restricted to FASS.

This creates an opportunity for applicants whose projects are interdisciplinary to identify another relevant academic unit that could contribute to their work.

Applicants should only identify a secondary affiliation where it has a meaningful connection to the proposed project.

Contacting an SFU Department Before Applying

Before submitting an application, candidates are strongly encouraged to contact the FASS department or unit with which they wish to work.

This is an important preparatory step.

Applicants can use the opportunity to discuss:

  • Their proposed project
  • The relevance of the project to the department
  • Potential academic connections
  • Their proposed primary affiliation
  • Possible secondary affiliations
  • Interdisciplinary opportunities
  • The fit between their project and SFU’s academic environment

Candidates can consult the official FASS departments and programmes list to identify the most appropriate unit.

Fellowship Duration

Applicants must indicate the length of fellowship they would like.

They must also explain why the requested duration is appropriate.

When determining the requested length, applicants should consider:

  • The scope of their project
  • Research requirements
  • Creative development
  • Writing requirements
  • Public engagement activities
  • Collaboration
  • Access to university resources
  • Expected project outcomes
  • The amount of work that can realistically be completed

The requested fellowship length should therefore be justified by the proposed project rather than selected without explanation.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027–28 Shadbolt Fellowship is:

October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m.

Applicants should ensure that their complete application package is submitted before the stated deadline.

Applications should be emailed to:

shadbolt_fellows@sfu.ca

Simon Fraser University states that a single PDF is preferred.

Applicants should also include their name in the filename.

For example:

FirstName_LastName_Shaddbolt_Fellowship_2027-28.pdf

Applicants should follow the official application instructions when preparing and submitting their documents.

Application Timeline

The official timeline for the 2027–28 fellowship is as follows:

September 21, 2026 — Online Q&A Information Session

An online question-and-answer information session will be held on September 21, 2026.

Time: 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Format: Online via Zoom

This session provides prospective applicants with an opportunity to learn more about the fellowship and ask questions before submitting their applications.

October 23, 2026 — Application Deadline

The complete application must be submitted by:

9:00 a.m. on October 23, 2026.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final minutes to submit their applications.

Late November — Shortlisted Candidates Notified

Shortlisted candidates are expected to be notified in late November.

December 7, 2026 — Reference Letters Deadline

For shortlisted candidates, reference letters must be submitted by December 7, 2026.

Applicants should therefore consider potential referees before the application deadline so they are prepared if shortlisted.

Important Eligibility Restrictions

Although the fellowship has broad eligibility in terms of professional background, SFU has identified important restrictions.

Current SFU Students

Individuals who are students at Simon Fraser University are ineligible for the fellowship.

Continuing SFU Appointments

Individuals who hold a continuing appointment at Simon Fraser University are also ineligible.

Relationship to Degree Requirements

SFU states that the project proposed for the fellowship will normally not be related to work being undertaken to fulfill the requirements of a degree programme in which the applicant is enrolled.

The fellowship project should therefore generally be independent from an existing degree requirement.

What Could Make an Application Strong?

While applicants should follow the official requirements rather than trying to predict the selection committee, a strong application should be clear, focused and closely aligned with the goals of the fellowship.

Present a Clearly Defined Project

Explain exactly what you want to accomplish during the fellowship.

The selection committee should be able to understand the project’s purpose, objectives, intellectual direction or creative contribution.

Demonstrate Humanities or Arts Relevance

Clearly explain how the proposed work contributes to the humanities and/or arts.

Explain the Broader Significance

Where appropriate, demonstrate how the project engages with important cultural, social, intellectual or public issues.

Show Why SFU Is a Good Fit

Explain why Simon Fraser University is an appropriate environment for the proposed work.

Identify the relevant primary unit and, where applicable, secondary affiliation.

Demonstrate Feasibility

The project should be realistic within the fellowship period requested.

Applicants should demonstrate that they have thought carefully about what they can accomplish during their time as a fellow.

Connect Your Experience to the Project

Your CV and cover letter should establish a logical connection between your previous experience and the proposed fellowship project.

Your past work should demonstrate that you have the skills, knowledge or creative experience necessary to undertake the project successfully.

Recommended Preparation Checklist

Applicants can prepare for the competition by following these steps:

  1. Read the official fellowship application form carefully.
  2. Develop a clear and meaningful fellowship project.
  3. Identify the most appropriate FASS department or unit.
  4. Consider whether a secondary SFU affiliation would strengthen the project.
  5. Contact the relevant department before submitting the application.
  6. Update your CV.
  7. Prepare a fellowship-specific cover letter.
  8. Clearly explain your desired fellowship duration.
  9. Review all eligibility restrictions.
  10. Complete the application form carefully.
  11. Combine the required documents into a single PDF where possible.
  12. Include your name in the PDF filename.
  13. Email the completed application to shadbolt_fellows@sfu.ca.
  14. Submit before October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m.
  15. If shortlisted, ensure that reference letters are submitted by December 7, 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Shadbolt Fellowship a scholarship?

No. It is a fellowship supporting emerging and established scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers in the humanities and arts.

Who is the fellowship designed for?

The fellowship is designed for engaged academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers working in the humanities and arts.

Can international applicants apply?

The announcement does not specify a nationality restriction, so the opportunity is not limited to Canadian applicants. International candidates may apply provided they satisfy the stated eligibility requirements.

Are Indigenous applicants encouraged to apply?

Yes. SFU explicitly states that the programme especially welcomes Indigenous applicants and supports work connected to decolonization and Indigenization.

Can current SFU students apply?

No. Individuals who are students at SFU are ineligible.

Can someone with a continuing SFU appointment apply?

No. Individuals who hold a continuing appointment at SFU are ineligible.

Do applicants have to be university professors?

No. The fellowship specifically includes artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers in addition to academic scholars.

Does the primary affiliation have to be within FASS?

Yes. Applicants are asked to identify their desired primary unit affiliation within the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences.

Can the secondary affiliation be outside FASS?

Yes. SFU states that secondary units may be any unit within Simon Fraser University.

Should applicants contact a department before applying?

Yes. SFU strongly encourages candidates to contact the FASS department or unit with which they wish to work before submitting their applications.

What documents are required?

Applicants must submit:

  • A fully completed application form
  • A current CV
  • A cover letter

A single PDF is preferred.

What is the application deadline?

The application deadline is October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m.

When will shortlisted candidates be notified?

Shortlisted candidates are expected to be notified in late November.

Official application page

Official 2027–28 application form

Conclusion

The Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship in the Humanities 2027–28 at Simon Fraser University provides an important opportunity for emerging and established academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers to develop meaningful work within a university environment dedicated to the humanities and arts.

The fellowship stands out because of its broad understanding of who can contribute to the humanities and arts. Applicants do not have to fit exclusively within the traditional academic model, as the programme welcomes artists, writers, practitioners and knowledge keepers alongside academic scholars.

The programme also places strong emphasis on creative practice, publicly engaged scholarship, critical engagement with major concerns of our time, decolonization and Indigenization. Indigenous applicants are particularly encouraged to apply, while candidates from underrepresented groups are also strongly encouraged to consider the opportunity.

Applicants should prepare a complete application consisting of the official application form, a current CV and a tailored cover letter. The cover letter should explain the proposed fellowship project, desired primary and secondary affiliations and the requested fellowship duration.

Candidates are also strongly encouraged to contact their preferred FASS department or unit before submitting their application.

The key deadline to remember is October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Shortlisted candidates are expected to be notified in late November, while reference letters for shortlisted candidates will be due on December 7, 2026.

For individuals whose work combines humanities, arts, culture, scholarship, creativity or public engagement, the Shadbolt Fellowship could provide a valuable platform to develop an ambitious project, engage with an academic community and contribute to broader intellectual, cultural and social conversations.

item.content:encoded:
The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR) Internship Program 2027 is offering students and recent graduates from Organization of American States (OAS) Member States an opportunity to gain practical professional experience in international human rights, law, communications, technology, translation, international cooperation, fundraising, and related fields.

The program provides participants with the opportunity to work alongside professionals and staff of the IACHR Executive Secretariat while developing a deeper understanding of the Inter-American human rights system and the mechanisms used to promote and protect human rights throughout the Americas.

For the upcoming 2027 Winter/Spring Session, applications are open from August 24 to September 11, 2026, while the internship itself will run from January 14, 2027, to April 30, 2027.

Importantly, the IACHR internship is unpaid, meaning participants should plan for their own living, travel, accommodation, and other expenses associated with participation.

IACHR Internship Program 2027 at a Glance

  • Program: IACHR Internship Program
  • Organization: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR)
  • Parent organization: Organization of American States (OAS)
  • Opportunity: Professional internship
  • 2027 Session: Winter/Spring Session
  • Locations: Washington, D.C. and National Offices
  • Application period: August 24 – September 11, 2026
  • Internship period: January 14 – April 30, 2027
  • Duration: Approximately three and a half months
  • Funding: Unpaid; no payment or stipend is provided
  • Eligible applicants: Students and recent graduates from OAS Member States
  • Primary fields: Law, international cooperation, fundraising, journalism, graphic design, web design, computer information technology, and translation
  • Application method: OAS Internship Program online application
  • Application requirement: Applicants must indicate their interest in the IACHR during the application process

What Is the IACHR Internship Program?

The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR) is a principal human rights body within the inter-American system. Its work focuses on promoting and protecting human rights in the Americas.

The IACHR Internship Program is managed in conjunction with the broader OAS Internship Program. It is designed to give young students and recent graduates an opportunity to gain first-hand experience with the work of the Commission and understand how the inter-American human rights protection system operates in practice.

Rather than being limited exclusively to law students, the program provides opportunities for people from several academic and professional backgrounds whose skills can contribute to the work of the Commission.

Participants have the opportunity to interact with professionals working within the IACHR Executive Secretariat and contribute to activities assigned during the internship.

This makes the program particularly valuable for individuals interested in careers involving:

  • International human rights
  • International law
  • Human rights advocacy
  • Public policy
  • International organizations
  • Diplomacy
  • Civil society
  • Journalism and communications
  • Digital communications
  • Graphic design
  • Web design
  • Information technology
  • Translation
  • International cooperation
  • Fundraising

IACHR Internship 2027 Application Deadline

The application window for the 2027 Winter/Spring Session is:

August 24 – September 11, 2026

Therefore, applicants interested in participating in the January 2027 to April 2027 session should complete and submit their applications during this period.

Important deadline

Application deadline: September 11, 2026

Applicants should not wait until the final day if they can submit earlier. The application process requires applicants to provide documentation, so prospective interns should review the requirements carefully and prepare their materials before beginning the online application.

When Will the Internship Take Place?

The selected interns for this session will participate from:

January 14, 2027 – April 30, 2027

The IACHR internship program operates according to established sessions and dates. Applicants should therefore ensure that they are available for the specified internship period before applying.

Individuals who need an internship to fulfill a specific university requirement should pay particular attention to the duration requirements.

The program states that participants fulfilling a university internship requirement for a specific length of time must provide documentation from their university confirming the required internship duration.

Where Is the IACHR Internship Based?

The 2027 Winter/Spring opportunity covers:

  • Washington, D.C.
  • National Offices

Washington, D.C. is particularly significant because it is home to the IACHR headquarters at:

1889 F Street N.W., Washington, D.C., U.S.A. 20006

Applicants should carefully review the OAS Internship Program information for the specific placement arrangements applicable to their application.

Who Can Apply for the IACHR Internship?

The program is aimed at students and recent graduates from OAS Member States.

The IACHR specifically identifies several categories of applicants who may be suitable for internship opportunities.

1. Law Students

Law students are among the primary groups targeted by the program.

This opportunity can be particularly relevant to students interested in:

  • International human rights law
  • International law
  • Public international law
  • Constitutional law
  • Human rights advocacy
  • Human rights litigation
  • Refugee and migration issues
  • International organizations
  • Regional human rights systems

Students interested in building a career in international human rights can potentially gain valuable exposure to how a regional human rights institution operates.

2. Recently Graduated Lawyers

The program also welcomes recently graduated lawyers.

For graduates who want to move into international human rights work, the internship can provide practical exposure that complements their academic legal training.

Experience at an international human rights institution can be relevant for future work with:

  • Human rights organizations
  • Civil society organizations
  • Government institutions
  • Ombudsmen’s offices
  • International organizations
  • Legal advocacy organizations
  • International law practices
  • Human rights litigation organizations

3. International Cooperation and Fundraising Students and Graduates

The IACHR also identifies opportunities for students and recent graduates working in international cooperation and fundraising.

This makes the program relevant beyond traditional legal careers.

Applicants with an interest in international development, institutional partnerships, resource mobilization, donor engagement, and international cooperation may find the experience particularly valuable.

4. Journalism Students and Recent Graduates

The IACHR Press Office receives students and recent graduates in journalism.

This provides an opportunity for communications-oriented applicants to gain experience in promoting awareness of human rights issues and communicating the work of an international institution.

Journalism applicants may benefit from exposure to:

  • Human rights communications
  • International affairs reporting
  • Institutional communications
  • Public information
  • Media relations
  • Human rights advocacy
  • Digital communications

5. Graphic Design Students and Graduates

The program also welcomes students and recent graduates in graphic design.

Graphic designers can potentially contribute to communications and promotional activities associated with the IACHR’s work.

This is particularly relevant for applicants who want to combine creative skills with international affairs and human rights communications.

6. Web Design Students and Graduates

The IACHR Press Office also offers opportunities for students and recent graduates with web design backgrounds.

This provides a potential pathway for individuals interested in using digital communication and web-based platforms to support human rights advocacy and public information.

7. Computer Information Technology Students and Graduates

The IACHR also receives students and recent graduates specializing in computer information technology.

This demonstrates that the internship program is not exclusively focused on legal or communications careers.

Applicants with technical skills may be able to gain experience within an international organization while applying their IT knowledge in support of institutional activities.

8. Translation Students and Graduates

The IACHR also provides opportunities for students and recent graduates in translation.

Translation applicants should be capable of working in at least two of the four official languages of the OAS:

  • English
  • Spanish
  • Portuguese
  • French

This requirement is especially relevant because the inter-American human rights system operates across multiple linguistic environments.

Which Countries Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for students and recent graduates from OAS Member States.

The Organization of American States is a regional organization bringing together countries from across the Americas. Therefore, eligibility is based on membership in the OAS rather than being restricted to a particular country or nationality within one subregion.

Applicants should verify that their country is an OAS Member State and review the official OAS Internship Program requirements before submitting an application.

The information provided for this opportunity does not establish a separate racial or ethnic eligibility requirement. The OAS also states that it is committed to equal employment opportunity and does not discriminate against individuals on the basis of race, color, marital status, religion, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or parental status.

What Will Interns Do?

During the internship, participants will have opportunities to work with professionals and staff from the Executive Secretariat of the IACHR.

Specific assignments are determined by the Executive Secretariat and may vary according to the needs of the Commission, the participant’s academic or professional background, and the particular internship placement.

The experience is therefore intended to provide practical exposure rather than simply classroom-based learning.

Depending on their field, interns may be exposed to activities connected to:

  • Human rights research
  • Legal and policy work
  • Human rights communications
  • Press and media activities
  • Graphic design
  • Web-related activities
  • Information technology
  • Translation
  • International cooperation
  • Fundraising
  • Other activities carried out by the Executive Secretariat

The exact duties are assigned by the IACHR.

Objectives of the IACHR Internship

The central objective of the internship is to provide eligible students and recent graduates with the opportunity to learn about the work of the Commission and gain practical training.

For law students and recent law graduates, this can mean gaining greater familiarity with the functioning of the inter-American human rights system.

The program can also help participants understand how human rights institutions interact with victims, civil society, governments, legal professionals, and other stakeholders.

The program’s objectives include:

  1. Providing practical professional training

    Participants gain experience working with professionals within an international human rights institution.

  2. Introducing participants to the IACHR’s work

    Interns can develop a better understanding of the Commission’s mandate and activities.

  3. Building knowledge of the inter-American human rights system

    Participants can learn how regional human rights protection mechanisms operate.

  4. Supporting professional development

    The knowledge and experience gained can contribute to future careers in human rights, law, international organizations, communications, technology, and related fields.

  5. Creating a multiplying effect in participants’ home countries

    One of the program’s broader objectives is for participants to take the knowledge they acquire during the internship back to their home countries and apply it professionally.

Why Is This Internship Valuable?

The IACHR internship can be particularly valuable because it combines academic knowledge with practical experience in an international institutional environment.

For a law student, for example, studying human rights law in university provides theoretical knowledge. Working alongside professionals at a regional human rights institution can provide a different perspective by showing how human rights mechanisms function in practice.

Similarly, a journalism student can gain insight into communicating human rights issues, while a graphic designer or web designer can see how creative and digital skills can support institutional advocacy.

The experience may therefore strengthen both technical and professional skills.

Professional development

Participants can develop skills that may be useful for future employment and further study.

International exposure

Working within the IACHR provides exposure to a major regional human rights institution.

Human rights knowledge

Participants can develop a deeper understanding of human rights protection mechanisms within the Americas.

Practical experience

The program provides an opportunity to move beyond academic study and gain hands-on experience.

Networking

Interns have the opportunity to work with professionals and staff of the IACHR Executive Secretariat.

Home-country impact

The program emphasizes the potential for participants to return home and use the knowledge acquired during their internship.

How the Internship Can Support a Future Career

The experience gained at the IACHR can be relevant to a wide range of professional pathways.

Former interns and fellows have gone on to work in areas including:

  • Human rights advocacy
  • Legal representation of victims
  • Civil society
  • International human rights organizations
  • Government institutions
  • Ombudsmen’s offices
  • Human rights litigation
  • International law
  • International development
  • Journalism
  • Communications
  • Technology
  • Translation
  • International cooperation

According to the program information, former participants have used their knowledge of the inter-American system in their home countries, including by representing victims of human rights violations, filing petitions and requests for precautionary measures with the Commission, advising civil society organizations, and working with government bodies and Ombudsmen’s Offices.

This illustrates the longer-term professional value that the program can potentially provide.

Is the IACHR Internship Paid?

No.

The IACHR Internship Program is unpaid.

The program is administered by the General Secretariat of the OAS, and the internship does not provide a salary, payment, or stipend.

This is an important consideration for international applicants, particularly those who may need to relocate or travel to Washington, D.C.

Applicants should therefore consider the financial implications of participating, including possible costs associated with:

  • International travel
  • Accommodation
  • Food
  • Local transportation
  • Visa or immigration-related expenses, where applicable
  • Insurance
  • Personal expenses

Prospective applicants should independently verify any additional financial or logistical requirements with the OAS before making travel arrangements.

How to Apply for the IACHR Internship 2027

Interested applicants must apply through the OAS Internship Program.

The electronic application becomes accessible during the designated application periods.

Applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Review the OAS Internship requirements

Before beginning the application, carefully review the eligibility criteria and documentation requirements for the OAS Internship Program.

Step 2: Prepare the required documents

Applicants should ensure that all documents requested by the OAS Internship Program are ready before submitting the application.

Step 3: Complete the online application

Submit the application through the OAS Internship Program’s electronic application system during the open application period.

Step 4: Indicate your interest in the IACHR

This is particularly important.

Applicants interested in an IACHR placement should clearly indicate their interest in the IACHR in the electronic application.

Step 5: Upload all required documentation

Applicants must upload the required supporting documentation to the electronic application form.

Step 6: Submit before the deadline

The application period for this session ends on:

September 11, 2026

Applicants should submit before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

Application Link

Applications are submitted through the OAS Internship Program’s electronic application system.

OAS Internship Application: http://www.oas.org/interns/

Applicants should also review the official OAS Internship Program webpage for the current requirements and application instructions.

See the OFY Website HERE for more internship programs

Important Information for University Students

Students who want to use the internship to satisfy a university requirement should pay special attention to the program’s duration rules.

The IACHR explains that participants who need to complete an internship of a specific length as part of their university requirements must provide documentation from their university specifying the required length.

Therefore, if your university requires you to complete a particular number of weeks or months, make sure you obtain the appropriate documentation before applying.

Official Languages of the OAS

The four official languages referenced by the program are:

  1. English
  2. Spanish
  3. Portuguese
  4. French

This is particularly important for translation applicants, who must be able to work in at least two of these four official languages.

Applicants in other fields should also recognize that multilingual ability can be highly relevant in an international and regional organization operating across the Americas.

Equal Employment Opportunity

The IACHR and OAS state that they are committed to equal employment opportunity based on individual merit.

The organization states that it does not discriminate against individuals on the basis of:

  • Race
  • Color
  • Marital status
  • Religion
  • Age
  • Gender
  • Disability
  • Sexual orientation
  • Gender identity
  • Parental status

Applicants should therefore be evaluated within the framework of the organization’s stated equal employment policy and the applicable internship requirements.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity may be particularly suitable for:

  • Law students interested in human rights
  • Recent law graduates
  • Students interested in international law
  • Graduates pursuing careers in human rights
  • International cooperation students and graduates
  • Fundraising students and graduates
  • Journalism students
  • Recent journalism graduates
  • Graphic design students and graduates
  • Web design students and graduates
  • Computer information technology students and graduates
  • Translation students and graduates who meet the language requirement
  • Young professionals interested in international organizations
  • Students seeking practical international human rights experience

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Although meeting the eligibility requirements is essential, applicants should also make sure their application clearly communicates why they are interested in the IACHR.

1. Clearly explain your field of interest

Connect your academic background or recent professional experience to the type of work carried out by the IACHR.

2. Demonstrate genuine interest in human rights

Applicants should be able to explain why human rights and the inter-American system are relevant to their academic or professional goals.

3. Highlight relevant experience

Where applicable, emphasize experience involving:

  • Legal research
  • Human rights
  • Policy
  • Advocacy
  • Journalism
  • Communications
  • Graphic design
  • Web design
  • IT
  • Translation
  • International development
  • Fundraising
  • Civil society

4. Show how the internship fits your career plans

A strong application should demonstrate that the internship is part of a broader professional development journey.

5. Pay attention to documentation

Incomplete applications or missing documents can create unnecessary problems. Review the OAS requirements carefully before submitting.

6. Apply early

Because the application period ends on September 11, 2026, applicants should prepare their materials in advance and avoid leaving submission until the last minute.

Key Dates to Remember

Applications open: August 24, 2026

Application deadline: September 11, 2026

Internship begins: January 14, 2027

Internship ends: April 30, 2027

Applicants should save these dates and make sure they can commit to the full internship period.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the IACHR Internship Program open to international applicants?

The program is intended for students and recent graduates from OAS Member States. Applicants should confirm that their country is an OAS Member State and review the current OAS internship eligibility requirements.

Is the IACHR internship paid?

No. The internship is unpaid and does not provide a payment or stipend.

When is the application deadline?

The deadline for the 2027 Winter/Spring Session is September 11, 2026.

When does the internship take place?

The internship runs from January 14, 2027, to April 30, 2027.

Do I have to study law to apply?

No. Although law students and recent lawyers are specifically mentioned, opportunities are also available for students and recent graduates in international cooperation and fundraising, journalism, graphic design, web design, computer information technology, and translation.

Can journalism students apply?

Yes. The IACHR Press Office receives students and recent graduates in journalism.

Can graphic designers apply?

Yes. Graphic design students and recent graduates are among the fields identified by the IACHR.

Can IT students apply?

Yes. The IACHR receives students and recent graduates in computer information technology.

What languages are relevant to the program?

The OAS has four official languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, and French. Translation applicants should be able to work in at least two of these languages.

Can a student use the internship to meet a university requirement?

Potentially, yes. However, if a university requires a specific internship duration, the applicant must provide documentation from the university specifying the required length.

Where do I apply?

Applicants should apply through the OAS Internship Program’s electronic application system and indicate their interest in the IACHR.

Final Takeaway

The IACHR Internship Program 2027 presents an opportunity for students and recent graduates from OAS Member States to gain practical experience within a major regional human rights institution.

Although the program is unpaid, its potential professional value extends beyond the internship period. Participants can gain practical exposure to the work of the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, interact with professionals in the Executive Secretariat, strengthen their understanding of regional human rights mechanisms, and develop experience that can support future careers in law, human rights, international organizations, communications, journalism, technology, translation, international cooperation, and related fields.

The opportunity is also broader than a traditional legal internship. Students and recent graduates in journalism, graphic design, web design, computer information technology, translation, international cooperation, and fundraising may also find relevant opportunities within the program.

For eligible applicants, the most important dates to remember are August 24 to September 11, 2026, when applications are accepted, and January 14 to April 30, 2027, when the internship takes place.

Anyone considering applying should carefully review the OAS Internship Program requirements, prepare all required documentation, clearly indicate their interest in the IACHR, and submit their application before the September 11, 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The PwC Reporting & Assurance – Intern – Summer 2027 opportunity offers students an opportunity to gain practical experience in sustainability reporting, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) analysis, assurance, data modeling, and climate and nature finance. The internship is designed for students pursuing or who have completed a bachelor’s degree in fields such as Accounting, Sustainable Resource Management, Environmental Science, or Finance. As an entry-level client service internship, the role provides exposure to PwC’s professional practices, sustainability reporting methodologies, client engagements, and assurance processes.

With sustainability reporting becoming increasingly important to organisations, this internship can provide students with practical exposure to how environmental, social, and governance information is collected, analysed, reported, and independently assessed.

The position is listed under Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) and carries Job ID 757093WD.

PwC Reporting & Assurance Intern Summer 2027 at a Glance

  • Position: Reporting & Assurance – Intern – Summer 2027
  • Organisation: PwC
  • Category: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG)
  • Employment level: Intern/Trainee
  • Job ID: 757093WD
  • Locations: Available in five locations, according to the provided listing; the specific locations are not identified in the supplied information
  • Salary range: $29.25–$48.00
  • Degree level: Bachelor’s degree
  • Minimum GPA: 3.0 overall
  • Preferred GPA: 3.5 overall
  • Typical academic level: Third year of a four-year degree or fourth year of a five-year degree at the time of application
  • Fields: Accounting, Sustainable Resource Management, Environmental Science, and Finance
  • Programme period: Summer 2027
  • Application deadline: No specific deadline is stated in the provided listing

About the PwC Reporting & Assurance Internship

The PwC Sustainability Reporting and Assurance internship focuses on projects designed to improve the credibility and quality of sustainability reporting, particularly information relating to environmental, social, and governance disclosures.

Interns will work within PwC’s Assurance practice and receive exposure to the methodologies and processes used by professional teams.

The position is structured as a learning-focused opportunity. Rather than expecting interns to enter the role as fully experienced professionals, PwC describes the internship as an opportunity to:

  • Learn about PwC’s practices
  • Gain exposure to professional work environments
  • Support project teams
  • Participate in sustainability-related projects
  • Observe experienced professionals
  • Develop communication skills
  • Ask questions and actively listen
  • Build an understanding of the business landscape
  • Develop a professional personal brand

This combination of practical participation and observation can help students understand how sustainability and assurance work is conducted in a professional services environment.

What Will a PwC Sustainability Reporting Intern Do?

The internship involves a variety of responsibilities connected to sustainability reporting, ESG data, assurance, climate finance, and organisational decision-making.

1. Support Sustainability Reporting Initiatives

Interns will support sustainability reporting activities by gathering and analysing information related to environmental, social, and governance metrics.

ESG metrics can involve different types of information used to understand an organisation’s sustainability-related performance and disclosures.

Through this work, interns can gain exposure to the processes involved in transforming organisational information into useful sustainability reporting.

2. Assist With Sustainability Reports

Interns will participate in preparing sustainability reports in alignment with established reporting standards, including:

  • Global Reporting Initiative (GRI)
  • Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)

This responsibility provides exposure to the frameworks and reporting practices used when organisations communicate sustainability and climate-related information.

3. Support Climate Finance and Nature Finance Projects

The role also involves assisting with the evaluation of climate finance and nature finance mechanisms.

This provides interns with an opportunity to explore how financial mechanisms can support sustainability projects and environmental objectives.

Students interested in the relationship between finance and sustainability may find this aspect of the internship particularly relevant.

4. Participate in Data Modeling and Analysis

Data plays an important role in sustainability reporting.

Interns will engage in data modeling and analysis to help generate insights that can support improvements in sustainability performance.

This responsibility makes analytical ability relevant to the position, particularly for students with backgrounds in finance, accounting, environmental science, or related disciplines.

5. Assist With Materiality Assessments

Interns will collaborate with teams conducting materiality assessments.

These assessments help organisations identify and prioritise significant ESG issues for reporting.

Through this work, interns can gain exposure to how organisations determine which sustainability issues are important enough to receive attention within reporting processes.

Exposure to Assurance and Auditing

A distinctive element of the internship is exposure to assurance work.

Interns will have opportunities to observe experienced auditors and learn about the processes involved in providing independent assessments.

This can help students understand how assurance professionals evaluate information and contribute to the credibility of organisational reporting.

For students interested in accounting, auditing, assurance, ESG, or sustainability reporting, this exposure can provide useful insight into professional practice.

Developing Technical Solutions for Sustainability Reporting

The internship also involves contributing to the development of technical solutions that can improve sustainability reporting processes.

This reflects the increasing role of technology and data in ESG reporting.

Interns may therefore gain exposure to how professional teams think about improving reporting processes through more effective technical approaches.

A Learning-Focused Internship

PwC emphasises that interns should approach the position with a learning mindset.

The internship is intended to help students understand PwC’s practices and methodologies while gradually contributing to team projects.

Important behaviours highlighted in the provided opportunity include:

  • Actively listening
  • Asking questions
  • Expressing ideas clearly
  • Learning from experienced professionals
  • Participating in team projects
  • Developing an understanding of business environments
  • Building a professional personal brand

This means applicants should not focus exclusively on technical qualifications. Their ability to learn, communicate, collaborate, and engage professionally is also relevant.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must currently be pursuing or have completed a Bachelor’s degree in one of the specified fields.

Eligible fields listed in the opportunity are:

  • Accounting
  • Sustainable Resource Management
  • Environmental Science
  • Finance

Applicants must also have an overall GPA of at least 3.0.

However, PwC states that a 3.5 overall GPA is preferred.

Academic Year Requirement

The opportunity is classified as an entry-level client service internship.

Candidates are typically expected to be:

  • In their third year of a four-year degree programme, or
  • In their fourth year of a five-year degree programme

at the time of application.

Students should therefore carefully consider their expected academic standing when determining whether the internship is appropriate for them.

What Sets Strong Applicants Apart?

In addition to the basic requirements, the listing identifies several characteristics that can strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Strong Academic Performance

Although the minimum GPA is 3.0, a 3.5 GPA is preferred.

Students with stronger academic performance may therefore be better positioned when competing for the internship.

CPA Eligibility

PwC also identifies meeting the educational requirements to sit for the CPA examination in the intended state of employment as a distinguishing factor before starting full-time employment at PwC.

This is particularly relevant to candidates pursuing accounting-related career paths.

Knowledge of Sustainability Reporting

Applicants who understand sustainability reporting standards and frameworks can distinguish themselves.

Familiarity with frameworks such as GRI and TCFD is particularly relevant because these are specifically referenced within the internship responsibilities.

Climate Finance and Reporting Experience

Experience participating in projects involving climate finance or reporting can also strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Data Analysis Skills

The ability to analyse data and use information to support decision-making is another valuable characteristic for this role.

Teamwork

The position involves collaboration with teams, making teamwork and the ability to contribute effectively to group projects important.

Artificial Intelligence

The listing also highlights the ability to leverage AI to create efficiencies, innovate ways of working, and deliver distinctive outcomes as a distinguishing characteristic.

Salary for the PwC Internship

The stated salary range for this position is:

$29.25–$48.00

The actual compensation within this range will depend on factors including:

  • Individual skills
  • Experience
  • Qualifications
  • Location
  • Applicable employment laws

Therefore, the salary should not be interpreted as a guaranteed single hourly or total compensation figure for every successful applicant.

PwC Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

PwC states that it is an equal opportunity employer.

According to the provided listing, qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to:

  • Race
  • Color
  • Religion
  • National origin
  • Sex
  • Pregnancy
  • Sexual orientation
  • Gender identity
  • Age
  • Disability
  • Genetic information
  • Veteran status
  • Marital status
  • Citizenship status
  • Other statuses protected by law

This means the listing does not establish a race-based restriction on eligibility.

  • Accounting
  • Finance

  • Assurance

ESG Analysis

Understanding and analysing environmental, social, and governance information.

Learning about the preparation of sustainability reports and relevant reporting standards.

Working with ESG-related data and using analysis to generate insights.

Observing how professionals provide independent assessments.

Practising the ability to express ideas clearly and communicate with professional teams.

Collaborating with colleagues on sustainability and reporting initiatives.

Exploring ways technology and AI can improve efficiency and create new approaches to professional work.
